This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $r\geq 3$. There exists $c_r>r^{-r}$ such that, for any $\epsilon>0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large, the following holds.
Any $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with at least $(1+\epsilon)(n/r)^r$ many edges contains a subgraph on $m$ vertices with at least $c_rm^r$ edges, where $m=m(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
#1075: [Er74c,p.80]
hypergraphs
Erdős [Er64f] proved that this is true with $c_r=r^{-r}$ whenever the graph has at least $\epsilon n^r$ many edges.

 so, define $\mathcal{F}_r$ to be the family of $r$-graphs obtained by starting with $K_{r,\dots,r}^{(r)}$ and adding one more hyperedge (crucially we must consider the entire family, since blowing up any $F\in \mathcal{F}_r$ will give a $((1/r)^r+\Omega(1))$-dense hypergraph which does not contain the other $F'\in \mathcal{F}_r\setminus \{F\}$). it would suffice to show $\text{ex}(n,\mathcal{F}_r)= ((1/r)^r+o(1))n^r$ (and this presumably is true). 
unfortunately I am not the most well-versed in extremal hypergraph stuff. perhaps somebody can finish it from here? (I tried to ask GPT 5 Thinking and Gemini 2.5 Pro about the $r=3$ case. but after several failures, I gave up.)

 Opus 4.8 suggests this is not true: the lemma ex(n, 𝓕₃) = (1/27 + o(1))n³ seems to be false, because the balanced blow-up of the 6-vertex 2-(6,3,2) design is 𝓕₃-free yet has density 5/108 · n³ > (1/27)n³ — so ex(n, 𝓕₃) is bounded below by a constant strictly above 1/27.

A full proof 
claimed by Qiyuan Gu (using GPT-6 Astra, GPT 5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5).
 Summary:
 We disprove Erdős Problem 1075 by constructing 16-uniform hypergraphs whose Lagrangians approach 16⁻¹⁶ from above, while all blow-ups have every subgraph below any prescribed density γ > 16⁻¹⁶. The construction uses a cyclic pair of link systems: closing the cycle gives a small gain, whereas opening it forces a larger quantitative loss, yielding the required Lagrangian bound.
